findings.location: Header, nav id="nav" element, lines 11 to 14, the page's only navigation mechanism
findings.evidence: nav id="nav" contains exactly two links, Plan a trip (href=/plan) and Accessibility (href=/accessibility); no search form, sitemap link, or breadcrumb trail appears anywhere else in the document.
findings.violation: The page offers only one mechanism for a reader to reach it, the primary navigation menu; WCAG-2.4.5 requires at least two independent mechanisms (search, sitemap, breadcrumb trail, or navigation menu) unless the page is one step in a linear process, and this rider service update page is a standalone content page, not a step in a checkout or similar linear flow.
findings.fix: Add a second, independent mechanism for reaching this page, such as a site search feature or a sitemap link, distinct from the existing primary navigation menu.

findings.location: Section 3, h2 id="s3-h" heading, line 34, text 'Fare adjustments'
findings.evidence: h2 id="s3-h" reads 'Fare adjustments'; the section it introduces also contains a div class="icon-delete" control labeled aria-label="Delete item", a wizard step reading 'Enter payment details', and a status-card div reading 'Riders can check real time arrivals at any station kiosk. Updates post to the schedule page within one business day.'
findings.violation: The heading 'Fare adjustments' does not describe most of what follows it: a delete control, a real time arrivals status card, and a status refresh button are unrelated to fare adjustments, so a reader scanning headings cannot predict what the section actually contains.
findings.fix: Split the section under headings that name its actual parts, for example a separate heading for the payment wizard and another for the status and report content, or move the unrelated content into the sections whose headings already cover that topic.
